replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's a fact that surprises most people: the AI reading your message right now has never seen a single word.

Not one. It sees numbers — only numbers — from the very first moment your prompt arrives.

**Tokenization** is the process that makes this happen. Before any "thinking" occurs, your text gets sliced into chunks called tokens, and each token gets mapped to a unique number.

Tokens aren't always whole words. "Unbelievable" might become three tokens: "Un", "believ", "able". A space before a word often becomes part of the token.

GPT-4 works with a vocabulary of roughly 100,000 possible tokens.

Here's a concrete example. The sentence "I went to the bank" might tokenize into five tokens: [40, 1816, 284, 262, 3331]. The model never sees letters — it receives that list of integers and works entirely from there.

This is why the AI can't "sound out" a word or notice a typo the way you do. It's not reading. It's processing a sequence of numbers.
